name: Primary Plasmacytoma of the Bone

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International Myeloma Working Group Criteria for Solitary Plasmacytoma

criteria.description: Presence of a single bone lesion with clonal plasma cells confirmed by biopsy
Bone marrow plasma cells less than 10% without evidence of systemic myeloma
No CRAB features (hyperCalcemia, Renal failure, Anemia, Bone lesions) attributable to systemic myeloma
No additional lesions on MRI or PET-CT outside the solitary plasmacytoma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Biopsy-proven solitary bone lesion with clonal plasma cells, bone marrow plasma cells <10%, and absence of systemic myeloma features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Exclusion of multiple myeloma is critical for diagnosis

searchTerms: single bone lesion with bone loss

pathognomonic.symptomName: Monoclonal plasma cell infiltration in bone biopsy
searchTerms: plasma cell buildup in bone biopsy
monoclonal plasma cells found in bone
abnormal plasma cell infiltration in bone tissue

common.symptomName: Localized bone pain at lesion site
Soft tissue mass adjacent to bone lesion
searchTerms: soft tissue lump next to bone lesion
tumor-like soft tissue swelling near bone
high levels of abnormal protein in blood
fatigue related to low red blood cells

rare.symptomName: Neurological deficits due to spinal cord compression
Renal impairment secondary to light chain deposition
searchTerms: kidney damage from light chain deposits
renal impairment due to protein buildup
kidney problems from light chain deposition

rare.symptomName: Systemic symptoms such as weight loss and night sweats
searchTerms: systemic symptoms like fever and sweating

laboratory: Serum protein electrophoresis showing monoclonal gammopathy
Bone marrow biopsy with <10% plasma cells
Normal calcium and renal function tests in most cases
imaging: MRI or PET-CT confirming absence of additional lesions
CT scan for lesion characterization and fracture risk assessment
genetic: Clonal plasma cells with typical cytogenetic abnormalities (e.g., t(11;14), del(13q)) in some cases
other: Histopathology confirming monoclonal plasma cell infiltration
Absence of CRAB criteria supporting solitary plasmacytoma diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of monoclonal plasma cells on biopsy
Absence of monoclonal protein in serum
Histology inconsistent with plasma cell neoplasm

redFlags: Rapidly progressive bone pain with neurological deficits
Signs of systemic myeloma such as anemia, hypercalcemia, or renal failure
references: International Myeloma Working Group consensus criteria for solitary plasmacytoma diagnosis
Orphanet: Primary plasmacytoma of the bone (ORPHA:100021)
Kyle RA, et al. Solitary plasmacytoma of bone and extramedullary plasmacytoma. Hematol Oncol Clin North Am. 1999
